propositions: JiraConfig accepts non-https jira.url silently without validation, risking credential exposure in transit; ReconcilerConfig validates scheme and rejects non-https unless allow_insecure is set.
JiraConfig lacks __post_init__ validation and allow_insecure field; config write path write_jira_config persists urls without scheme validation, allowing cleartext urls to be persisted.
Multiple consumers of load_config().jira swallow ConfigError to degrade to env-only (resolve_jira_settings, _jira_onboard._detect), bypassing validation that should be fail-loud per rebar's posture.

A generalized _validate_https_url function should be introduced and reused by both ReconcilerConfig (renamed wrapper _validate_reconciler_tls) and new JiraConfig.__post_init__ to reject non-https schemes unless allow_insecure=True.

resolve_jira_settings must re-raise InsecureUrlError before the existing ConfigError degrade handler to enforce fail-loud for non-https jira.url, while _jira_onboard._detect intentionally degrades to keep the recovery wizard usable.

write_jira_config must validate https-only before persisting (fail-closed on cleartext urls) so the onboarding wizard cannot silently write a non-https url, and jira.allow_insecure must be registered as a config coercer mirroring reconciler.allow_insecure.
